correctness.rationale: For each n>=3, a mixed independent colour class is necessarily exactly {a_i,b_i}. Two pure opposite-side blocks of sizes >=2 produce a two-coloured 4-vertex path except when both coincide as one two-index block. The resulting exhaustive partition dichotomy gives an explicit summation; the Stirling subset decomposition and binomial convolution yield every coefficient. The minimal class count and its multiplicity follow by exact size analysis. An adjacency-based direct brute-force checker independently tests 1,189,120 proper partitions for 2<=n<=7 and the coefficients agree throughout, but finite checks are not the proof for all n.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior assertion chi_s=n means only that some n-class partition exists and that no smaller count works. It neither specifies 1+binom(n,2) optimum partitions nor determines the Stirling counts at each larger palette size. The class-wise structural argument is additionally required. Related strong-odd and proper conflict-free colourings use genuinely different admissibility rules and do not logically dominate this enumeration.

originality.rationale: The exact crown-graph scalar optimum n is prior art (Mary--Bibi--Julietterayan, 2017). In the inspected closest original paper, its Theorem 4.11 gives the scalar and one coloring but not a class-count sequence, a Stirling formula, or the n!*(1+C(n,2)) named optimum multiplicity. The 2023 regular-graph work gives degree-dependent bounds and uniqueness complexity, not these explicit counts. No mathematically stronger covering statement was identified in the accessible full-text material or comparable publicly indexed results. This is an evidence-based self-review, not proof of priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper, thesis, sequence database or alternate-name paper may independently derive the same Stirling coefficients or the optimal-partition count.
No independent bibliographic priority verification has been performed.

value.rationale: The invariant is a full palette-dependent polynomial, not a single chromatic number. It describes the entire distribution of all feasible star-colour partitions of a natural dense regular bipartite family and finds a complete two-type classification and exact 1+binom(n,2) multiplicity of optimal classes, a nontrivial refinement of a previously known scalar result. All coefficients have a closed Stirling/binomial formula, enabling exact probabilistic counting and comparisons at every palette size.
